# Use case 6: comparative genomics with species and phylogenetic profile graphs

In comparative genomics, data are often represented as matrices with
features (e.g., gene families, orthogroups, synteny clusters) in rows and
species in columns. Here, we will use __GraphExperiment__ to store a
matrix of *phylogenomic profiles* (i.e., copy number of synteny clusters
across species) along with two graphs: a species-species graph derived
from a phylogeny (in `colGraphs`), and a graph of synteny clusters with
similar phylogenetic profiles (in `rowGraphs`). We will use data from the
__syntenet__ package [@almeida2023syntenet], which include synteny network
clusters for 25 eudicot species from @zhao2019network, and a
microsynteny-based angiosperm phylogeny [@zhao2021whole].

We will also demonstrate how phylogenies (`phylo` objects) can be
represented as `igraph` objects, since phylogenies are a special
kind of graph (i.e., a directed acyclic graph, DAG).

```{r here}
#| message: false
#| eval: true

library(here)
library(GraphExperiment)
library(syntenet)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggraph)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(ape)

set.seed(123) # for reproducibility
```

## Data description

The data set `clusters` is a data frame with genes and the synteny clusters
they belong to, and the species tree `angiosperm_phylogeny` is a `phylo`
object with 123 angiosperm species. We will first create a phylogenomic
profiles matrix with the copy number of each synteny cluster across species.

```{r}
# Load data
data(clusters)
data(angiosperm_phylogeny)

head(clusters)
angiosperm_phylogeny

# Get phylogenomic profiles
profiles <- phylogenomic_profile(clusters)
profiles <- matrix(profiles, nrow = nrow(profiles), dimnames = dimnames(profiles))
rownames(profiles) <- paste0("SC", rownames(profiles))
profiles[1:5, 1:5]
```

Species in the profiles matrix are represented by abbreviations,
while species in the tree are represented by their full names. Thus, we
will create a data frame with species metadata (full names and families),
and keep only species that are present in both data sets.

```{r}
# Create species metadata
species_md <- tribble(
    ~abbrev, ~species, ~family,
    "adu", "Arachis duranensis", "Fabaceae",
    "car", "Cicer arietinum", "Fabaceae",
    "cca", "Cercis canadensis", "Fabaceae",
    "fve", "Fragaria vesca", "Rosaceae",
    "gma", "Glycine max", "Fabaceae",
    "hlu", "Humulus lupulus", "Cannabaceae",
    "jcu", "Jatropha curcas", "Euphorbiaceae",
    "Lang", "Lupinus angustifolius", "Fabaceae",
    "lja", "Lotus japonicus", "Fabaceae",
    "lus", "Linum usitatissimum", "Linaceae",
    "mdo", "Malus domestica", "Rosaceae",
    "mes", "Manihot esculenta", "Euphorbiaceae",
    "Mnot", "Morus notabilis", "Moraceae",
    "mtr", "Medicago truncatula", "Fabaceae",
    "pbr", "Pyrus x bretschneideri", "Rosaceae",
    "pmu", "Prunus mume", "Rosaceae",
    "ppe", "Prunus persica", "Rosaceae",
    "ptr", "Populus trichocarpa", "Salicaceae",
    "pvu", "Phaseolus vulgaris", "Fabaceae",
    "rco", "Ricinus communis", "Euphorbiaceae",
    "tpr", "Trifolium pratense", "Fabaceae",
    "van", "Vigna angularis", "Fabaceae",
    "vra", "Vigna radiata", "Fabaceae",
    "Zjuj", "Ziziphus jujuba", "Rhamnaceae"
) |>
    filter(species %in% angiosperm_phylogeny$tip.label) |>
    column_to_rownames("species")

nrow(species_md)

# Keep only species in both data sets and rename columns to full names
profiles <- profiles[, species_md$abbrev]
colnames(profiles) <- rownames(species_md)

# Remove synteny clusters that are absent from all remaining species
profiles <- profiles[rowSums(profiles) > 0, ]

# Quick look at the final profile matrix
dim(profiles)
profiles[1:5, 1:5]
```

## Phylogenies as graphs

A phylogeny is a DAG in which edges point from ancestors to descendants.
Thus, `phylo` objects can beconverted to `igraph` objects with
the `as.igraph()` method from __ape__ [@paradis2019ape]. Here,
we will first subset the tree to keep only our species of interest,
and then convert it to a DAG with branch lengths as edge attributes.

```{r}
# Subset tree and remove node labels (bootstrap support values)
tree <- ape::keep.tip(angiosperm_phylogeny, colnames(profiles))
tree$node.label <- NULL

# Convert `phylo` to `igraph`, adding branch lengths as edge attributes
dag <- ape::as.igraph.phylo(tree, directed = TRUE)
E(dag)$length <- tree$edge.length
V(dag)$is_tip <- V(dag)$name %in% tree$tip.label

dag
is_dag(dag)
```

Since the tree is now an `igraph` object, any graph algorithm can be used
on it. For instance, we can obtain the matrix of shared evolutionary
history between pairs of species (i.e., the distance from the root to
their most recent common ancestor), which is the variance-covariance matrix
under a Brownian motion model used by most phylogenetic comparative methods.
For tips $i$ and $j$, the shared path length is
$(d_{root,i} + d_{root,j} - d_{i,j}) / 2$, where $d$ is the distance
between nodes along branches.

```{r}
# Get distances between all pairs of nodes
d <- distances(dag, mode = "all", weights = E(dag)$length)
root <- V(dag)[igraph::degree(dag, mode = "in") == 0]$name
tips <- V(dag)$name[V(dag)$is_tip]

# Get shared path lengths
shared <- outer(d[root, tips], d[root, tips], "+") / 2 - d[tips, tips] / 2

# Sanity check: same as the output of `ape::vcv()`
all.equal(shared, ape::vcv(tree)[tips, tips])
```

Nodes of graphs in `colGraphs` must match column names (here, species)
*exactly*. Thus, DAGs representing phylogenies (which include
internal nodes) cannot be stored in the `colGraphs` slot.
Instead, we will store a species-species graph with edge weights
representing shared evolutionary history (i.e., the off-diagonal elements
of the matrix above), and a node attribute (`root_distance`) with the
distances from the root to each species (i.e., the diagonal). Pairs of
species whose most recent common ancestor is the root share no evolutionary
history (weight of zero), so they are not connected.

::: {.callout-note}
Native support for graphs containing nodes that are not observations
(e.g., internal nodes of phylogenies and phylogenetic networks) is planned for
future versions of __GraphExperiment__. For now, full DAGs can be stored in
the `metadata` slot, as we will do below.
:::

```{r}
# Create species graph from the matrix of shared path lengths
phylo_graph <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
    shared, mode = "undirected", weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE
)
V(phylo_graph)$root_distance <- diag(shared)[V(phylo_graph)$name]

phylo_graph
```

## Phylogenetic profile similarity graph

Synteny clusters (or gene families) with similar patterns of presence and
absence across species (i.e., similar phylogenetic profiles) are likely
functionally related, as genes in the same pathway or protein complex tend
to be gained and lost together [@pellegrini1999assigning]. Here, we will
create a graph of synteny clusters by connecting clusters with Jaccard
similarities $\geq$ 0.9 between their presence/absence profiles. Since
clusters present in (nearly) all species or in very few species provide
little information, we will only consider clusters that are absent
in at least three species and present in at least three species.
All other clusters will be included in the graph as isolated nodes,
since nodes in row graphs must match row names *exactly*.

```{r}
# Get presence/absence profiles of informative clusters
pa <- (profiles > 0) * 1
n_species <- ncol(pa)
informative <- rowSums(pa) >= 3 & rowSums(pa) <= n_species - 3
sum(informative)

# Get Jaccard similarities between informative clusters
jaccard <- 1 - as.matrix(dist(pa[informative, ], method = "binary"))
jaccard[jaccard < 0.9] <- 0

# Create graph, including all clusters as nodes
profile_graph <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
    jaccard, mode = "undirected", weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE
) |>
    add_vertices(
        sum(!informative), name = rownames(pa)[!informative]
    )

profile_graph
```

We will then identify modules (or communities) of synteny clusters with similar
profiles using the Louvain algorithm.

```{r}

# Identify modules of clusters with similar profiles (Louvain algorithm)
modules <- as.character(membership(cluster_louvain(profile_graph)))
modules[igraph::degree(profile_graph) == 0] <- NA # isolated nodes are not in modules
V(profile_graph)$module <- modules

profile_graph
```

## Storing all data in a `GraphExperiment` object

Now, we can store the phylogenomic profiles, the species metadata, and both
graphs in a `GraphExperiment` object. The full DAG of the phylogeny will be
stored in the `metadata` slot.

```{r}
ge <- GraphExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = profiles),
    colData = species_md[colnames(profiles), ],
    rowGraphs = list(profile_sim = profile_graph),
    colGraphs = list(phylo = phylo_graph),
    metadata = list(phylo_dag = dag)
)

ge
```

As expected, node attributes from `rowGraphs` and `colGraphs` were
added to `rowData` and `colData`, respectively.

```{r}
head(rowData(ge))
head(colData(ge))
```

## Phylogenetic signal of synteny clusters

Finally, we will use the species graph in `colGraphs` to quantify the
phylogenetic signal in the copy number of each synteny cluster, i.e.,
to what extent closely related species have similar copy numbers.
For that, we will calculate Moran's I [@gittleman1990adaptation], using
as weights the shared evolutionary history between species, which we
can extract directly from the graph as a weighted adjacency matrix.

```{r}
# Get weight matrix from the species graph
W <- as_adjacency_matrix(colGraph(ge, "phylo"), attr = "weight", sparse = FALSE)
W <- W[colnames(ge), colnames(ge)]

# Calculate Moran's I for each cluster with variable copy number
counts <- assay(ge, "counts")
variable <- apply(counts, 1, var) > 0
moran <- apply(counts[variable, ], 1, function(copies) {
    res <- ape::Moran.I(copies, W)
    c(I = res$observed, P = res$p.value)
})
moran <- as.data.frame(t(moran))
moran$padj <- p.adjust(moran$P, method = "BH")

# Add results to `rowData`
rowData(ge)$moran_I <- moran[rownames(ge), "I"]
rowData(ge)$moran_padj <- moran[rownames(ge), "padj"]
head(rowData(ge))

# Number of clusters with significant phylogenetic signal
sum(rowData(ge)$moran_padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
```

Synteny clusters with phylogenetic signal include, for instance, clusters
that are specific to (or lost in) particular lineages. Since the results
of the Moran's I test and the module assignments in the phylogenetic profile
graph are both in `rowData`, we can easily check which modules contain more
clusters with significant phylogenetic signal.

```{r}
# Modules with the largest number of clusters with phylogenetic signal
rowData(ge) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    filter(moran_padj < 0.05, !is.na(profile_sim__module)) |>
    count(profile_sim__module, sort = TRUE) |>
    head()
```

Let's visualize the copy number of synteny clusters with significant
phylogenetic signal, with species ordered as in the phylogeny and
clusters grouped by module in the phylogenetic profile graph.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-dpi: 300

# Subset object to keep only clusters with phylogenetic signal
ge_signal <- ge[which(rowData(ge)$moran_padj < 0.05), ]

# Get species order from the phylogeny (stored in `metadata`)
species_order <- intersect(
    names(dfs(metadata(ge)$phylo_dag, root, mode = "out")$order),
    colnames(ge_signal)
)

# Keep only the 5 largest modules for visualization
top_modules <- names(sort(table(rowData(ge_signal)$profile_sim__module), decreasing = TRUE))[1:5]
mod <- rowData(ge_signal)$profile_sim__module
mod[!mod %in% top_modules] <- "Other"
mod[mod != "Other"] <- paste0("M", mod[mod != "Other"])

# Plot heatmap
family_colors <- setNames(
    palette.colors(length(unique(ge$family)), "Okabe-Ito"),
    unique(ge$family)
)
Heatmap(
    pmin(assay(ge_signal, "counts")[, species_order], 5),
    name = "Copy number",
    col = c("white", "#fee0d2", "#fc9272", "#de2d26", "#a50f15", "#67000d"),
    cluster_columns = FALSE,
    row_split = factor(mod, levels = c(paste0("M", top_modules), "Other")),
    show_row_names = FALSE, show_row_dend = FALSE, cluster_row_slices = FALSE,
    row_title_rot = 0,
    top_annotation = HeatmapAnnotation(
        Family = ge$family[match(species_order, colnames(ge))],
        col = list(Family = family_colors)
    ),
    column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 9, fontface = "italic")
)
```

The heatmap shows that modules in the phylogenetic profile graph
group synteny clusters with lineage-specific patterns of presence/absence
(e.g., clusters that are specific to or lost in Fabaceae or Rosaceae).
With all data in a single object, comparative genomics analyses that
combine feature-level graphs (e.g., co-occurring gene families) and
species-level graphs (e.g., phylogenies) become straightforward.
